subphase: systematic stale-blocked audit: safe declarations already in source

summary.statement: 26 BLOCKED UNSAFE_FN_DEF rows whose current declaration is already safe. 8 have a compile-time coercion control; 18 have no build-time control because the row slot type accepts both safe and unsafe fn pointers, so the safe declaration itself is the elimination evidence. s2i_poison is deliberately excluded: it is already discharged by boundary-sweep-B54, and a second non-discharging boundary would block that discharge.

method: enumerate every BLOCKED UNSAFE_FN_DEF row in boundary-sweep-B*.json and *-sites.json; resolve the operation span at S; reject any candidate whose declaration still contains `unsafe`; locate the compile-time coercion control

negative_control.observation: those control consts require a safe fn; restoring `unsafe` fails to type-check

non_claims: Does not cover blocked rows whose declaration is still unsafe.
The 18 rows without a control are eliminated because the declaration is safe, not because a control proves it.

control_gap.why: the X509V3ExtI2s/I2v/R2i/S2i slot types accept `unsafe extern "C" fn`, so the static row initialiser coerces either form; no build-time control exists for these declarations
control_gap.effect: a future edit could restore `unsafe` without a build failure; recorded, not claimed controlled
